articles.title: When a Meteorite Punched Through a Roof, It Delivered a Salty Secret About Life's Origins
articles.summary: A rare CM1/2 carbonaceous chondrite crashed into a New Jersey home in 2024. Its pristine salt-rich fragments reveal ancient asteroid brines — a crucial clue to how water shaped the chemistry that may have led to life.

articles.title: Thumbnail-Sized Bird Figurines from 40,000 Years Ago Reveal Ice Age Artists' Keen Eye
articles.summary: Two miniature mammoth ivory birds, each under half an inch, were unearthed in Germany's Hohle Fels cave. Dating to the Aurignacian period, they offer a rare glimpse into how early humans observed and depicted the natural world.

articles.title: New Study Challenges Advice to Cut Sweet Foods: Sweetness Itself Isn't the Enemy
articles.summary: A six-month trial found no difference in taste preferences or health markers between high, low, and average sweetness diets. Researchers say sugar and calorie density, not sweet taste, should be the focus of dietary guidance.
